passage:
After residents worried about water quality, the town invited students to watch public testing. Scientists collected samples from different points and explained each step.
Students learned that clear water is not automatically safe. Some problems cannot be seen or smelled.
The town posted results online and held a question meeting.
Trust improved because people saw the process, not only the final numbers.
The project showed that science communication matters. Data locked in a report may not calm fear. Showing how data is collected helps people understand why it can be trusted.
Transparency can be as important as testing itself.
